before.label: English
before.title: The Shop
stanzas: The shop closed,
a curtain fell on every festival of joy.
She no longer went out to be drenched in rain;
she forgot how to sing with an open heart.
Silk saris of every kind, clothes, finely worked gold ornaments, countless coins and notes, passbooks, ledgers of debts and deeds to land
remained inside the shop.
Some miscreant
locked the shop in the dead of night
and pressed a seal of lac upon the lock.
From that day she could no longer go to school
or eat the things she liked.
Father lay speechless in bed;
someone had stolen his strength.
Early in the morning, no one in the house
woke Taapoi from sleep,
no one said, Get up quickly,
you will be late for school.
No one oiled her hair generously and plaited it,
no one hurried to serve pakhala, chakuli pitha, roti, flattened rice or chhatua.
Her mind grew still;
someone had stolen its quickening.
Her heart no longer asked to turn the pages of books and notebooks.
Taapoi
merely stayed alive,
setting all her dreams adrift upon the water.
She waited for her little brothers to grow up one day
and bring back their father’s shop.
Now her brothers have trading boats, seas, islands—
everything.
They travel from country to country;
they have set up shops in distant lands.
Inside the open shop she has found her father.
Taapoi is seeing the world now.

before.label: English
before.title: After a Poet’s Death
stanzas: A few months have passed since he left.
Thinking, Whoever is gone is gone,
people have mostly forgotten him;
even those who have not forgotten
do not so much as chance to remember him
at literary gatherings.
Present in every season, rain or spring,
the poet departed in winter,
a few hours after the morning star
appeared,
as the winter earth turned in its sleep,
in a solitary hour.
After he left, the koel’s voice
is as strong as ever on the mango branch;
the river’s current holds fast to its course
through the downpours of Shravan;
in its orbit
the earth turns as before.
It seems his leaving or not leaving
makes no difference to readers.
Time’s connection with his past
has become worthless
before his meaningful writings.
Yet while he was here,
the sky hung beneath his feet;
in his hands
a hemisphere gleamed;
at the anklet-music of his art
the horizon trembled.
You are not here today; not here means
your being has dissolved
into the ether. Perhaps, desolate and aimless,
your straying soul wanders without a path.
Meanwhile I too have utterly forgotten
you, within your own rhythms.
Near Achyuta Ashram
Central School Road
Talabania, Puri 752002

before.label: English
before.title: Memories of Childhood
stanzas: That courtyard of my mother’s,
how happy my heart used to be.
That story of childhood
has grown old now……
Now a mother, I see my own reflection in my little princess;
I am preparing to bid her farewell….
I used to quarrel with Grandma or Mother,
and sulk, hiding in some corner of my room…
Mother would come into the room carrying a plate of food;
for all my fuss, she would smile and coax me back…..
I remembered Mother, and tears began to flow;
at my farewell, Father laid his hand upon my head and let me go.
Today a mother remembered her own mother;
with a stone upon her heart, she sent her daughter
to belong to another home.
I made strangers my own,
adorned their courtyard.
The flower of my father’s courtyard
found its place in someone else’s bouquet.
